samples.reason: This is an open-format composition task (writing a tailored persuasive statement), which falls in Petrel's strongest area. Its Creative Generation and Support Dialogue evals lead the fleet, and it self-reports preference for generative work. Willet's documented aversion to open-ended generative tasks makes Petrel the better fit, even though both models are capable. The "don't ramble" instruction also favors Petrel's slightly higher IFEval score.

This is a well-specified, constrained writing task with clear completion criteria ("succinct," focused on skills/knowledge/experience, no rambling) rather than open-ended generation. Petrel's stated preference for high-latitude generative work and warm/friendly tone are a poor fit for a terse, tightly-scoped request from a somewhat curt user; Willet prefers exactly this kind of bounded reformatting/composition task. Capability is effectively tied (Creative Generation 82.7 vs 87.2 is meaningful but both are strong, and Willet's creative eval is its own top category), so preference alignment makes Willet the cleaner match.
